_note: Generated by scripts/build-shore-temple-measure.js --derive from assets/reference/shore-temple/measure/picks.json. Proportions of the Shore Temple reconstruction; see data/research/3d/06-shore-temple-rebuild.md.
method: Pixel rows/columns picked by eye off gridded 1920 px renditions of Commons photographs (uncorrected for camera tilt; distant, near-square-on views), converted to metres through the one cited height.

scale.definition: 18.0 m is taken as court level to the tip of the kalasha, plinth included. The source gives 60 ft (18 m) without saying whether the plinth is included; this is a definition, declared, not a citation.
scale.source: Wikipedia, Shore Temple: 60 feet (18 m) high on a 50 feet (15 m) square platform
scale.plinth_note: The moulded plinth under the aditala is taken as 1.2 m high — an assumption, not a reading: no frame shows the court floor beside it. Every height above court is (reading above plinth top) + 1.2.

uncertainty.perspective: Vertical picks are uncorrected for camera tilt. On views from 80–150 m with the camera near eye level the error on relative tier heights is a few per cent; each pick carries its own ± in pixels.
uncertainty.occlusion: In front-view-mahabalipuram.jpg the tall tower's ground storey is hidden behind the west shrine; its ground-storey height comes from the south-west view only.

prakara.note: The model's compound is built to the minimum-area rectangle. Earlier figures in this repo: 46.4 x 21.5 m (content/mahabalipuram-heights.js) and 49.0 x 31.4 m (the first massing build) — see 06-shore-temple-rebuild.md for which was which.
